pages.privacy.15: Kagemura is a strategy game with cartoon combat, rated for teens and up in the app stores. Before you play online, the game asks your year of birth (and the month, only when the year alone does not settle it) without suggesting an answer, or uses the age range your device's app store provides. It keeps only the resulting age group (under 13, 13 to 17, or 18 or older), not your date of birth, and uses it only to set up the game for your age:

pages.privacy.21: Your village is saved on your device. The game does not need an account, and with online play off it sends nothing about you to us (unless you turn on crash reports, below). Gameplay statistics shown in Settings ("Analytics events") stay on the device, unless you are an adult playing online and choose to share them (below). If you play in a web browser, the website that delivers the game sees your IP address, as every website does.
pages.privacy.22: What we collect, why, and on what legal basis
pages.privacy.23: The legal bases are those of the EU and UK GDPR (Art. 6) and of Brazil's LGPD (Art. 7). "Contract" means we need the data to provide the game you asked to play; "legitimate interests" means we have weighed our reason against your rights and you can object (see "Your rights").
pages.privacy.24: Online account: random Player ID, a secret sign-in token (we store only a one-way hash), the name you choose, your friend code, your age group, your privacy choices, when you were last online
pages.privacy.25: To run your online account, show your name to other players and apply the protections for your age group. Basis: contract; for the age group also legal obligation and legitimate interests (protecting younger players). LGPD: contract performance, legal obligation.
pages.privacy.26: Your game: your base for raids, the village kept on our server and the actions you take in it, battles and replays, honor, rankings and ratings, a history of resources added or spent
pages.privacy.27: So online play works, raids are checked and fair, and you can continue on another device. Basis: contract; checking battles for cheating is a legitimate interest.
pages.privacy.28: Social features: Alliance and Gang chat messages, warrior requests and gifts, friends and friend requests, Gangs, Gang Wars and Friendly Duels
pages.privacy.29: To provide these features. Basis: contract.
pages.privacy.30: Safety: reports you make (reason, optional note and, for a chat message, its text as it was sent), blocks, mutes and suspensions, and the notices we send you about them (kept in your account until it is deleted)
pages.privacy.31: To keep the community safe, act on reports, tell reporters and affected players what we decided, and handle appeals. Basis: legitimate interests (a safe game for everyone) and, where online-safety laws require it, legal obligation.
pages.privacy.32: Sign-ins you link (optional): the id that Apple, Google or Game Center gives us for you; for Sign in with Apple also the token Apple issues to the game; which sign-in each of your devices used and when it was last used
pages.privacy.33: To restore your account on another device, sign out devices when you unlink a sign-in, and revoke the game's access at Apple when you delete your account or unlink Apple. We never receive or keep your email address or name from them. Basis: contract, at your request.
pages.privacy.34: Purchases: the store's transaction id, product, price, date and refund status
pages.privacy.35: To deliver each purchase once, restore it, handle refunds and apply the under-18 limit. Basis: contract and legal obligation (tax and accounting records).
pages.privacy.36: Notifications (optional): your device's notification token, the types you chose and your time-zone offset
pages.privacy.37: To send only the notifications you switched on, never at night or too often. Basis: consent (you turn them on, and can turn them off).
pages.privacy.38: Network data: your IP address with each request to our server
pages.privacy.39: To stop abuse (rate limits) and keep the service secure. Kept only in short-lived counters and in server logs. We do not use it to work out where you are. Basis: legitimate interests (security).
pages.privacy.40: Server error reports: the error, the route, and the request method and path (no query strings or request contents)
pages.privacy.41: To fix faults in our server. Basis: legitimate interests.
pages.privacy.42: Crash reports from the game (optional, below)
pages.privacy.44: Play statistics (optional, adults only, below): what you do in the game under a random statistics id
pages.privacy.45: To see where players get stuck and whether changes help. Basis: consent.
pages.privacy.46: Support email and web deletion requests
pages.privacy.47: To answer you and carry out your request, and to keep a record that we did. Basis: legitimate interests; for deletion requests, legal obligation.
pages.privacy.48: If you ask the game to find your Game Center friends, we use their ids once to see which of them play Kagemura; we do not keep that list. We do not make decisions about you by automated means that have legal or similarly significant effects. One automatic safety step exists: a chat message reported by three different players is hidden until our staff look at it.
pages.privacy.49: Play statistics (off unless you say yes; adults only)
pages.privacy.50: When you play online and have told us you are an adult, the game asks once whether you want to share play statistics; Settings has the same switch. It is off until you say yes, and the game never asks, or sends statistics, for players under 18 or whose age it does not know. When it is on, the game sends what you do in the game (sessions starting, tutorial steps, raids with their stars and destruction, upgrades and research started, offers shown, Jade spent on speed-ups and purchases with their product and price) under a random statistics id made for this purpose. The statistics id is not your Player ID and is never sent together with it; the game does not add your name, village, chat or sign-in token, and our server does not store the IP address with them. Saying yes also sends what this device recorded before (so we can see the first minutes of play). Turning the switch off deletes what that statistics id sent; saying yes again starts a new one. We keep shared statistics for 400 days and use them only in totals (for example, how many new players came back the next day). Players who share may receive slightly different timings for in-game offers, to compare which works better; prices, rewards and game rules are the same for everyone. Some versions of the game also send your time zone's offset from UTC (for example, two hours ahead), never the name of the time zone or your location, so that days can be counted on your own calendar; it is kept with the statistics id and deleted with it.
pages.privacy.51: Crash reports (off unless you turn them on)
pages.privacy.52: Versions of the game that include crash reporting show a "Send crash reports" switch in Settings. It is off until you turn it on. When it is on and the game hits an error, the game sends the error message, where in the game's code it happened, the game version and the platform to our error-tracking service (Sentry). The game does not attach your name, Player ID, village, chat or save, and removes web-address parameters and anything shaped like an email address from the message. An error message can still occasionally include text the game was working on when it failed. The service sees the IP address the report comes from; we set the service not to store IP addresses. Turning the switch off stops new reports at once.
pages.privacy.54: When you report a message or a player, our staff review it and can remove the message, mute chat or suspend the account (see the {t0}community rules{t1}). We tell the player who reported what happened, and we tell a player when we remove their message, mute them or suspend them, with the reason and how to appeal. We do not tell a reported player who reported them. Every staff action is logged so that decisions can be checked.
pages.privacy.56: {t0}Support email.{t1} If you write to us, we receive your email address and what you send, and use them only to answer you and keep a record of that answer.
pages.privacy.57: {t0}Web deletion requests.{t1} The account deletion page asks for your Player ID, the deletion code the game gives you, and an optional note. It does not ask for an email address. We keep the request and what we did about it as a record that it was handled.
pages.privacy.59: We do not ask for your email address in the game, and we do not collect your contacts, precise location, photos or advertising id. There are no ads and no third-party tracking, and we do not sell your data or share it for advertising or cross-context behavioural advertising.
pages.privacy.61: We use service providers who process data only on our instructions: our hosting provider (server and database: {t0}{t1}), our error-tracking service Sentry (crash reports only if you turn them on, and our server's own errors; data region: {t2}{t3}), and Apple and Google (sign-in, purchases and notifications, under their own privacy policies). Our staff see what they need to answer support and moderate.
pages.privacy.62: Some of these providers may process data outside your country, including outside the EU, UK or Brazil. Where data leaves the EU or UK for a country without an adequacy decision, we rely on the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses (and the UK addendum or International Data Transfer Agreement) or another transfer mechanism the law allows. You can ask us for a copy of the safeguards.

pages.privacy.69: Server logs with IP addresses: {t0}{t1}. Rate-limit counters: at most an hour.
pages.privacy.70: Support email: {t0}{t1} after the last message.

pages.privacy.79: Wherever you live, you can ask us to:
pages.privacy.80: {t0}access{t1} your data and get a copy, and receive the data you gave us in a commonly used, machine-readable form ({t2}portability{t3});

pages.community.4: Kagemura is a game for a general audience, played by people of many ages, countries and languages. By using online play you agree to these rules. Breaking them can get messages removed, chat muted or an account suspended.
pages.community.5: These rules are part of the {t0}{t1}.
pages.community.7: No harassment, bullying, threats or hate, in any language, spelling or code word.
pages.community.8: No sexual content, and nothing that sexualises or endangers children.
pages.community.9: No names that insult, impersonate another player, staff or a real person, or pretend to be official.
pages.community.10: No spam, advertising, scams, or links to cheats.
pages.community.11: Do not share personal details: yours or anyone else's (real name, address, phone, school, social accounts). Never ask other players for them.
pages.community.13: Before online play, the game asks for your year of birth (or uses the age range your phone's app store shares) and keeps only an age group, never the date.
pages.community.14: Players under 13 chat with ready-made messages only, keep the name the game gave them, and can be found only by friend code.
pages.community.15: Players aged 13 to 17 start hidden from strangers (only friends of friends can find them by name) and with their online status hidden; they can change this in Friends → Privacy. Offers never pop up for players under 18, and they have a monthly spending limit.
pages.community.16: An age group can only be made stricter in the game. If it is wrong, contact support.
pages.community.18: No cheating: no modified games, bots, scripts or tools that play for you or change battles. Our server checks battles and refuses ones it cannot reproduce.
pages.community.19: Do not exploit bugs. Tell us about them instead ({t0}support{t1}).
pages.community.20: Do not buy, sell or share accounts, or trade game items for real money.
pages.community.21: Do not use other people's payment methods, or refund purchases you used in order to keep them.
pages.community.23: {t0}Block{t1}: tap {t2}⋯{t3} next to a message, a member or a friend card. You stop seeing their chat and requests at once, and they can no longer find you or send you friend requests.
pages.community.24: {t0}Report{t1}: from the same {t2}⋯{t3} menu, choose a reason and, if you like, add a note. A message reported by three different players is hidden for everyone until staff decide.
pages.community.25: If someone is in danger, contact your local emergency services first.
pages.community.27: Staff review reports and can remove messages, mute a player's chat and suspend accounts. Every staff action is logged. When we act, the player affected gets a message in the game (Settings → Online play → Account) saying what we decided, the reason and how to appeal, and everyone who reported it hears the outcome. If you think we got it wrong, write to {t0}{t1} with your Player ID and we will look again.
pages.community.28: The chat and name filters catch common bad words only; they cannot catch everything in every language. Reports and blocks are how players help us with the rest.

pages.account.4: Open {t0}Settings → Online play → Account → Delete online account{t1}. Your online account is deleted at once. This works even if you switched to {t2}Play offline{t3}: the game connects just to delete it.
pages.account.6: Your player name and online account, the base you shared for raids, and your village if it is kept on our server.
pages.account.7: Your friends and friend requests, your Gang membership and your linked sign-ins.
pages.account.8: Raids on your village, your Alliance membership, your chat messages, warrior requests and warriors sent to you.
pages.account.10: Replays of raids you made stay with the players you raided, shown as "Deleted player". Warriors you sent and Alliance War results stay the same way, without your name.
pages.account.11: Copies of your base in other players' recent battles are removed within 30 days.
pages.account.12: A village saved on your device stays there: to remove it, uninstall the app, or clear the game site's data in your browser. Purchase records are kept without your Player ID, as tax and refund rules require.
pages.account.14: Other players can see Player IDs, so we need proof that the account is yours: a {t0}deletion code{t1}. Get one in the game under {t2}Settings → Online play → Account → Get a deletion code{t3} (it works once, for 30 days), then send it here with your Player ID from the same screen. Staff delete a request with a valid code within 30 days, usually much sooner.
pages.account.15: No code, and you can't open the game any more? Send your Player ID anyway and contact support from the game's support page with the reference you get: we can only delete the account once we can confirm it is yours (for example through the Apple, Google or Game Center sign-in linked to it, or a store receipt). We don't ask for an email address here.
